Time-Domain Simulation

Complete guide to dynamic simulation in Powerful.jl.

Basic Workflow

Time-domain simulation requires three steps: solve power flow, add dynamics, and simulate.

using Powerful, PowerFlowData, DifferentialEquations

# Step 1: Solve power flow
case = PowerFlowData.parse_network("cases/ieee14.raw")
sys_pf = SystemModel(case)
pf_prob = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys_pf)
pf_sol = solve(pf_prob, NewtonRaphson())

# Step 2: Parse dynamic models
dyr_data = parse_dyr("cases/ieee14.dyr", sys_pf)

# Step 3: Create and solve TDS problem
prob = TDSProblem(sys_pf, pf_sol, dyr_data; tspan=(0.0, 10.0))
sol = solve(prob)

See Getting Started for explanation of power flow steps.

Understanding the Transition

From Power Flow to TDS

Power flow computes steady-state algebraic equations:

0 = g(y)  # Algebraic: power balance

TDS adds differential equations for dynamics:

dx/dt = f(x, y, t)  # Differential: generator dynamics
0 = g(x, y, t)      # Algebraic: network equations

Key concepts:

  • x: Differential states (rotor angle δ, speed ω)
  • y: Algebraic variables (voltage V, angle θ)
  • DAE: Differential-Algebraic Equations

Model Replacement

Dynamic models replace their static counterparts:

Static ModelDynamic ModelVariables Added
PV GeneratorGENCLSδ (angle), ω (speed)
Slack BusGENCLSδ, ω

The TDS system contains:

  • Dynamic models (GENCLS) with differential states
  • Remaining static models (PQ loads, branches)
  • All network equations

TDSProblem Construction

All-in-One Constructor (Recommended)

# Automatic initialization from power flow
prob = TDSProblem(
    sys_pf,                          # Power flow system
    pf_sol,                          # Power flow solution
    dyr_data;                        # Dynamic models from parse_dyr
    tspan = (0.0, 10.0),             # Simulation time
    formulation = PowerInjection()   # DAE formulation
)

What it does:

  1. Creates links between dynamic and static models
  2. Filters replaced static models
  3. Initializes dynamic states from power flow
  4. Constructs TDS-ready system

Staged Construction (Inspectable)

For explicit control and debugging intermediate results:

# Phase 1: Prepare TDS system (links dynamic → static models)
tds_sys = TDSSystem(sys_pf, pf_sol, dynamic_models)

# Inspect linking results
println(tds_sys.links.source_type)  # [:GENCLS, :GENCLS, ...]
println(tds_sys.links.target_idx)   # Which static instance each replaces

# Phase 2: Initialize states from power flow
init = TDSInitialization(tds_sys)

# Debug: check initial conditions
@show init.dyn.GENCLS.omega   # Should be ~0.0 (synchronous speed deviation)
@show init.dyn.GENCLS.delta   # Rotor angles from power flow

# Phase 3: Create problem
prob = TDSProblem(tds_sys, init; tspan=(0.0, 10.0))

When to use:

  • Debugging initialization failures
  • Customizing intermediate results (e.g., modify init.dyn.GENCLS.delta before creating problem)
  • Testing stages independently

Solving TDS Problems

Default Solver

sol = solve(prob)  # Uses Rodas5P by default

Rodas5P is a 5th-order L-stable Rosenbrock method optimized for DAEs with mass matrices.

Explicit Solver Selection

# Rosenbrock methods (good for stiff systems)
sol = solve(prob; alg=Rodas5P())
sol = solve(prob; alg=Rodas4P())

# For very stiff systems
sol = solve(prob; alg=Rodas5())

DAE Formulation

Disable mass matrix to use implicit DAE solvers:

sol = solve(prob; use_mass_matrix=false, alg=IDA())

When to use: For systems where Rosenbrock methods fail.

Solver Comparison

SolverTypeUse Case
Rodas5PRosenbrockDefault, stiff systems
Rodas4PRosenbrockLess stiff, faster
IDAImplicit DAEVery stiff, convergence issues

Solver Options

Tolerances

sol = solve(prob;
    abstol = 1e-8,   # Absolute tolerance
    reltol = 1e-6    # Relative tolerance
)

Trade-off: Tighter tolerances → more accurate but slower.

Time Stepping

sol = solve(prob;
    dt = 0.01,        # Initial time step
    dtmin = 1e-6,     # Minimum step size
    dtmax = 0.1       # Maximum step size
)

Saving Options

# Save at specific times
sol = solve(prob; saveat=0.0:0.01:10.0)

# Save only start and end
sol = solve(prob; save_everystep=false)

# Dense output (interpolation between steps)
sol = solve(prob; dense=true)

Events and Disturbances

Events allow you to introduce disturbances during simulation—branch trips, load changes, setpoint modifications, etc.

Defining Events

Events are specified when creating the TDSProblem:

prob = TDSProblem(
    sys_pf, pf_sol, dyr_data;
    tspan = (0.0, 10.0),
    events = [
        BranchTrip(1.0, 1, 5, "1"),    # Trip line 1-5 at t=1.0s
        BranchClose(2.0, 1, 5, "1"),   # Reconnect at t=2.0s
    ]
)

Built-in Event Types

Branch Trip/Close:

BranchTrip(time, from_bus, to_bus, circuit)   # Disconnect branch
BranchClose(time, from_bus, to_bus, circuit)  # Reconnect branch

The circuit ID must match exactly (including spaces if present in data file).

Custom Events with FieldModification

For events not covered by built-in wrappers, use FieldModification directly:

events = [
    # Halve generator inertia at t=3.0
    FieldModification(3.0, :GENCLS, (101, "1"), :H, :multiply, 0.5),

    # Increase load P by 10 MW at t=5.0
    FieldModification(5.0, :PQ, (3, "1"), :p, :add, 10.0),

    # Set branch status to offline
    FieldModification(1.0, :Branch, (1, 5, "1"), :st, :set, 0.0),
]

FieldModification parameters:

  • time: When to apply (seconds)
  • model: Target model type (:Branch, :PQ, :GENCLS, etc.)
  • key: Instance identifier tuple (from model's composite key)
  • field: Field to modify (:st, :p, :H, etc.)
  • operation: :set, :add, or :multiply
  • value: Value for operation

Model Keys

Each model uses a composite key for identification:

ModelKey FieldsExample
Bus(i,)(101,)
Branch(i, j, ckt)(1, 5, "1")
PQ(i, id)(3, "1")
GENCLS(i, id)(101, "1")

Complete Example with Events

using Powerful, PowerFlowData, DifferentialEquations

# Load and solve power flow
case = PowerFlowData.parse_network("cases/ieee14.raw")
sys = SystemModel(case)
pf_sol = solve(ACPowerFlowProblem(sys), NewtonRaphson())

# Parse dynamics
dyr_data = parse_dyr("cases/ieee14.dyr", sys)

# Define disturbance sequence
events = [
    BranchTrip(1.0, 1, 5, "1"),    # Trip at t=1.0s
    BranchClose(2.0, 1, 5, "1"),   # Reconnect at t=2.0s
]

# Create and solve
prob = TDSProblem(sys, pf_sol, dyr_data;
    tspan = (0.0, 5.0),
    events = events
)
sol = solve(prob)

# Plot results to see disturbance response
data = collect_state_trajectory(sol, prob)

For implementation details, see Developer: Events.

Accessing Results

Solution Status

println("Success: $(sol.retcode == :Success)")
println("Time steps: $(length(sol.t))")
println("Final time: $(sol.t[end])")

Differential States (TDS-Specific)

Extract all differential states (δ, ω) as a structured table:

# Get as NamedTuple (works without DataFrames)
data = collect_state_trajectory(sol, prob)
println(data.GENCLS_delta_1)  # Access specific variable

# Convert to DataFrame if needed
using DataFrames
df = DataFrame(data)

Automatic naming: model_variable_instance

  • GENCLS_delta_1 → GENCLS[1].delta
  • GENCLS_omega_2 → GENCLS[2].omega

Save to CSV:

using CSV, DataFrames
data = collect_state_trajectory(sol, prob)
CSV.write("tds_results.csv", DataFrame(data))

Variable metadata:

# Get information about state variables
state_info = get_state_variable_info(prob)

for info in state_info
    println("$(info.model).$(info.variable)[$(info.instance)] @ address $(info.address)")
end

Direct access by index:

# Access by position in state vector
delta_1 = [u[1] for u in sol.u]  # First state variable
omega_1 = [u[3] for u in sol.u]  # Third state variable

Plotting:

using Plots

# Extract specific states
data = collect_state_trajectory(sol, prob)

# Plot generator angles
plot(data.t, data.GENCLS_delta_1, label="Gen 1 δ")
plot!(data.t, data.GENCLS_delta_2, label="Gen 2 δ")
xlabel!("Time (s)")
ylabel!("Rotor Angle (rad)")

Algebraic Variables (Shared API)

TDS solutions also contain algebraic variables (voltage, angle, currents) accessible using the same API as power flow.

Note: TDS solution u is a combined vector [x; y] where:

  • x: Differential states (extracted above)
  • y: Algebraic variables (accessed below)

The solution object doesn't directly support get_var - you must extract the DAE workspace to access algebraic variables during time-stepping. For post-processing, use the final state.

For complete algebraic variable access API, see Accessing Results.

Formulations

TDS supports the same formulations as power flow.

PowerInjection (Default)

Network equations in polar form:

prob = TDSProblem(sys_pf, pf_sol, dyn_models;
                  formulation=PowerInjection())

When to use: Default choice for most systems.

CurrentInjection

Network equations in rectangular form:

prob = TDSProblem(sys_pf, pf_sol, dyn_models;
                  formulation=CurrentInjection())

When to use: Better numerical conditioning near voltage collapse.

Both formulations give identical results. See Power Flow Analysis for details.

Dynamic Models

GENCLS - Classical Generator

Simple swing equation model:

States:

  • delta (δ): Rotor angle relative to reference
  • omega (ω): Rotor speed deviation from synchronous speed

Parameters:

  • M: Inertia constant (MWs/MVA)
  • D: Damping coefficient (pu)

Equations:

dδ/dt = ω
M·dω/dt = P_m - P_e - D·ω

Where:

  • P_m: Mechanical power (from power flow P_gen)
  • P_e: Electrical power (computed from network)

Initialization:

  • δ₀ computed from power flow voltage angle
  • ω₀ = 0 (synchronous speed)
  • P_m set to match power flow active power

Advanced Topics

Mass Matrix Formulation

TDS uses mass matrix formulation for efficient solving:

M·dx/dt = f(x, y, t)
0 = g(x, y, t)

Where M is a sparse diagonal matrix:

  • M[delta, delta] = 1
  • M[omega, omega] = M (inertia constant)

Why: Avoids division by M in residual evaluation, better numerics.

Architecture

TDS uses the unified ADCache architecture shared with power flow:

prob = TDSProblem(...)  # Problem specification with initialization
sol = solve(prob)        # Solving creates ADCache + adapters internally

Key components:

  • TDSProblem: System structure, time span, formulation, initial states
  • ADCache: Stateless core for residual evaluation (shared with power flow)
  • TDSAdapter: Unified adapter for DifferentialEquations.jl interface (supports both ODE and DAE formulations via strategy pattern)

Unified Adapter Design: The TDSAdapter uses a strategy pattern with evaluate! dispatch:

  • evaluate!(du, adapter, u, t, ODEInterface()) - For Rosenbrock/Rodas solvers
  • evaluate!(resid, adapter, du, u, t, DAEInterface()) - For IDA/DFBDF solvers

Benefits:

  • Single evaluation engine for both power flow and TDS
  • Single adapter type serving both ODE and DAE interfaces
  • Automatic differentiation support through shared workspace
  • Zero duplication between static and dynamic simulation

See Computation Architecture for implementation details.

Addressing Strategy

Control memory layout for sparse factorization:

prob = TDSProblem(sys_pf, pf_sol, dyn_models;
                  addressing=AMDAddressing())

When to use: Large systems (>1000 buses) where factorization dominates.

Common Issues

Solver Fails to Converge

Symptoms: Warning about dt < dtmin, solution truncated.

Causes:

  • Poor initialization
  • System instability (fault clearing issues)
  • Too-large time steps

Solutions:

  1. Check power flow converged properly
  2. Reduce initial time step: dt=0.001
  3. Tighten tolerances: abstol=1e-10, reltol=1e-8
  4. Try different solver: alg=Rodas5()
  5. Use DAE formulation: use_mass_matrix=false, alg=IDA()

Incorrect Initial Conditions

Symptoms: Large transient at t=0, or immediate divergence.

Causes:

  • Power flow not at equilibrium
  • Mismatch between static and dynamic models

Solutions:

  1. Verify power flow converged: pf_sol.converged == true
  2. Check generator powers match between PF and dynamics
  3. Validate initialization quality:
result = validate_tds_initialization(prob)
print_validation_report(result)
# Should show max residuals < 1e-6

Memory Issues

Symptoms: Out of memory for large systems.

Solutions:

  1. Use sparse saving: save_everystep=false, saveat=0.0:0.1:10.0
  2. Disable dense output: dense=false
  3. Reduce tolerance slightly: abstol=1e-6

Complete Example

using Powerful, PowerFlowData, DifferentialEquations
using CSV, DataFrames, Plots

# Load and solve power flow
case = PowerFlowData.parse_network("cases/ieee14.raw")
sys_pf = SystemModel(case)
pf_prob = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys_pf)
pf_sol = solve(pf_prob, NewtonRaphson())

if !pf_sol.converged
    error("Power flow did not converge")
end

# Parse dynamics
dyr_data = parse_dyr("cases/ieee14.dyr", sys_pf)

# Create and solve TDS problem
prob = TDSProblem(
    sys_pf,
    pf_sol,
    dyr_data;
    tspan = (0.0, 10.0)
)

sol = solve(prob; saveat=0.0:0.01:10.0)

if sol.retcode != :Success
    @warn "Simulation did not complete successfully: $(sol.retcode)"
end

# Extract and save results
data = collect_state_trajectory(sol, prob)
CSV.write("results.csv", DataFrame(data))

# Plot generator angles
plot(data.t, data.GENCLS_delta_1, label="Gen 1")
plot!(data.t, data.GENCLS_delta_2, label="Gen 2")
xlabel!("Time (s)")
ylabel!("Rotor Angle (rad)")
savefig("generator_angles.png")
